title: 9.1 The Pythagorean Theorem

icans: I can use the Pythagorean Theorem to find a missing side of a right triangle.
I can tell whether three lengths form a Pythagorean triple.
I can use the converse of the Pythagorean Theorem to decide whether a triangle is right, acute, or obtuse.

vocab: the side __________ from the right angle; the longest side of a right triangle
the two sides that form the __________ angle
three ___________ integers a, b, and c with c² = a² + b²
if c² = a² + b², then the ___________ is a right triangle

blocks.sec: Part 1 · Discovery: is it a right triangle?

blocks.p: Partner A draws each triangle (longest side as the base) and measures the largest angle. Partner B finds a² + b² and c², where c is the longest side.
When a² + b² = c², the largest angle is ______________.

blocks.sec: Part 2 · Notes and examples (fill in each note, then work the example)

notes: Pythagorean Theorem: in a right triangle, the square of the length of the _______________ equals the sum of the squares of the lengths of the _______________: c² = a² + b².
Pythagorean triple: three positive _______________ a, b, c with c² = a² + b². Common ones: 3, 4, 5; 5, 12, 13; 8, 15, 17; 7, 24, 25.

blocks.stem: Find the value of x. Then tell whether the side lengths form a Pythagorean triple.
Find the value of x. Then tell whether the side lengths form a Pythagorean triple.
A 16-foot ladder leans against a wall. The bottom of the ladder is 5 feet from the wall. How high up the wall does the ladder reach? Round to the nearest tenth.

notes: Converse of the Pythagorean Theorem: if c² = a² + b² (c the longest side), then the triangle is a _______________ triangle.

notes: Acute or obtuse: with c the longest side, if c² < a² + b² the triangle is _______________; if c² > a² + b² it is _______________.
